actions.findings:
Meta-strategy approaches, involving adaptive selection among exploration strategies, optimize empirical success in resource-constrained intelligent systems. [source-c38a2230f18a448b]

Unmanaged autonomous services (e.g., in urban mobility) suffer from balancing failures, illustrating the necessity for intrinsic goal-generation mechanisms in non-stationary environments. [source-eea91700e4df42aa]
actions.limitations: Current findings focus on theoretical and specific application domains rather than generalized autonomous discovery processes. Cognitive architecture integration remains a bottleneck for real-world deployment.
actions.next_questions: Can the identified meta-strategy approaches be mapped to open-ended agent architectures to enable spontaneous goal generation?
actions.reason: Synthesizing new evidence into the notebook allows for a more robust understanding of how agent limitations and environment non-stationarity influence autonomous inquiry.
actions.summary: Autonomous systems require self-generated goals and open-ended learning mechanisms to acquire flexible skills in unpredictable environments. Analysis of resource constraints suggests meta-strategies for exploration, while urban mobility models reveal the failure modes of unmanaged systems in non-stationary settings.
actions.title: Autonomous Problem Formulation via Hybrid Architectures and Goal Generation

proposal.summary: This research iteration advances the autonomous problem formulation inquiry by integrating findings on resource-constrained exploration strategies and the dynamics of non-stationary urban environments, synthesizing these as indicators of how autonomous agents might evaluate problem significance.
